title: Contents Packout & Storage Custody Loss and Damage Compensation
content:
Custody credits compensate a Contents Packout & Storage customer for one inventoried item lost or damaged in the company's custody.

## Rule

1. The job must be in returned or invoiced status when a custody credit is posted.
2. A custody credit may be posted only when the loss or damage is reported no later than the damage report window after the contents were returned.
3. The damage report window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the job's returned date, and a report made on the last day of the window is in time.
4. Each inventoried item takes at most one custody credit.
5. The item must appear on the job's inventory by its barcode tag.
6. A lost item is compensated at its actual cash value and a damaged item at the lesser of its repair cost and its actual cash value, in either case never more than the tier's custody liability cap per item; when the customer bought declared-value coverage, the cap is replaced by the item's share of the declared value.
7. Items listed on a signed disposal authorization are never compensated.
8. A report after the window, or a claim above the cap, is handed to a human representative as not covered by policy.

## The report window

The clock starts from the returned date recorded on the job, the day the contents were returned. Day 1 of the window is the day after that returned date; the window runs for the tier's damage report days (the tier figure on the product's custody terms), counted in calendar days, and a report made on the last day is in time.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical 6-day window).** Contents returned on the 10th of a month: day 1 is the 11th and the last day is the 16th. A report on the 16th is in time; a report on the 17th is after the window.

## Amount of a custody credit

| Item | Amount | Upper limit |
|---|---|---|
| lost | its actual cash value | the tier's custody liability cap per item, or, where the customer bought declared-value coverage, the item's share of the declared value |
| damaged | the lesser of its repair cost and its actual cash value | the same limit |
| listed on a signed disposal authorization | never compensated | — |

## Conditions shown by the records

- The job's status (returned or invoiced) and its returned date, as the company record shows them.
- The item appears on the job's inventory by its barcode tag, and no custody credit already stands for that tag on the job.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A damaged item with a repair cost of 180.00 and an actual cash value of 260.00, on a hypothetical cap of 300.00 with no declared-value coverage, is compensated at 180.00, the lesser of the two figures and within the cap.
